cities.base: A casa particular in Habana Vieja between Plaza Vieja and the Capitolio, or in Vedado near Calle 23 if you want quieter nights; book one that says it has an inverter or generator and a water tank, and
cities.name: Havana

cities.base: Any casa on or just off Calle Salvador Cisneros, the one main street; every house is a casa with a porch and a rocking chair, breakfast is 5 to 7 dollars, and the owner books your horses, guide and Ca
cities.name: Viñales

cities.base: A colonial casa within three blocks of Plaza Mayor so you can walk the cobbles home from the music steps in the dark; many have roof terraces. Havana to Trinidad by colectivo is 5 to 6 hours and 40 to
cities.name: Trinidad

cities.base: Punta Gorda, the peninsula south of the centre, for casas on the water and the sea breeze when the power is off; the centre around Parque Martí is a 25 minute walk or a 2 dollar bicitaxi. Trinidad to
cities.name: Cienfuegos

cities.base: A beach casa in the village of Playa Larga at the head of the bay; the owners cook lobster dinners and call the dive centre for you. It is 95 km and about 1 hour 45 from Cienfuegos by taxi (35 to 45 d
cities.name: Playa Larga (Bay of Pigs)

cities.base: Do it as a day from Cienfuegos (67 km, 75 minutes, 40 to 50 dollars for a taxi there and back with waiting time) or as the stop on a Trinidad to Havana transfer day; the Che complex and the train are
cities.name: Santa Clara

places.name: The four plazas of Habana Vieja
places.note: Plaza Vieja, Plaza de San Francisco, Plaza de Armas and Plaza de la Catedral in that order, then Obispo to the Capitolio; the restored core is intact and quiet now, and two blocks off it the buildings are collapsing.

places.name: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes, Arte Cubano
places.note: The Cuban-only building on Trocadero, three floors from colonial portraits to 1980s conceptualism, air conditioned when the grid is up; Sundays it shuts at 14:00.

places.name: Malecón, Prado to Hotel Nacional
places.note: Three kilometres of sea wall where the city comes to sit when the power is off; walk it at sunset, not after dark, and do not go in the Hotel Nacional at the end, it is on the Prohibited Accommodations list and you cannot legally spend money there.

places.name: Callejón de Hamel Sunday rumba
places.note: Salvador González's painted alley hosts live rumba every Sunday from noon; it is real drumming and it is also a tourist event, so arrive at 11:30 for a spot and watch your pockets.

places.name: Fábrica de Arte Cubano
places.note: A converted oil factory with galleries, three stages and bars, still the best night in Havana and still Thursday to Sunday; it takes an annual break of several weeks in late summer, runs on generators, and you pay a tab card on the way out.

places.name: La Guarida
places.note: The paladar in the Fresa y Chocolate staircase building on Concordia, running since 1996 with its own generator; the food is good rather than great, the rooftop bar is the reason to book, and reserve by email a week out.

places.name: Paladar Los Mercaderes
places.note: Up a petal-strewn staircase on Mercaderes, a family-owned dining room with a violinist and a menu that actually has what it lists; the lobster is the dish, and lunch is easier to get than dinner.

places.name: Paladar Doña Eutimia
places.note: Ropa vieja and frozen mojitos in a tiny room on Callejón del Chorro off Plaza de la Catedral; eight tables, so put your name down in person at noon for a 13:00 seat.

places.name: Grados
places.note: A chef-owned house restaurant on Calle E with a short menu that changes with what the market had that morning, which in 2026 is the honest way to cook here; walkable from FAC territory, message ahead on WhatsApp.

places.name: El Cañonazo, Fortaleza de San Carlos de la Cabaña
places.note: The nightly 9pm cannon from the fortress across the harbour, 15 dollars in taxis there and back; the ramparts at dusk are the point and the ceremony is over in a quarter hour.

places.name: Fusterlandia
places.note: José Fuster's mosaic-covered house and the streets of the fishing suburb around it, 25 minutes west by taxi (about 30 dollars return); the family runs it, so the entry money counts as support for Cubans, and pair it with lunch in Miramar.

places.name: El Floridita
places.note: State-run Hemingway daiquiri bar with a bronze of him at the counter, a queue and a band playing to phones; it is not on the Restricted List but it is not where your money should go, and the same goes for the Bodeguita del Medio.

places.name: Mirador Los Jazmines
places.note: The postcard view of the whole valley from the roadside terrace 3 km south of town, best at 7am with mist in the fields; stand on the public overlook, not in the state hotel behind it.
places.neighborhood: Carretera a Pinar del Río, km 25

places.name: Valle del Silencio horse ride
places.note: Booked through your casa the night before, 5 to 6 dollars an hour per horse plus the guide; ask for the loop with the tobacco house and the lake, and go at 8 before the heat.

places.name: Finca Raúl Reyes
places.note: A working tobacco farm a 20 minute walk north of the church where the family rolls in front of you and sells the 90 percent they keep from the state; buy a few cigars here rather than the boxes in Havana.

places.name: Los Acuáticos hike
places.note: A 250 m climb on a farm track to a hamlet on the mogote with coffee on the porch and the valley below; a casa-arranged guide costs 10 to 15 dollars and is worth it for the turnings.

places.name: Cueva del Indio
places.note: A lit cave walk, then a motorboat out along the underground river, one way, 40 minutes all in, daily 09:00 to 17:00. Wanderlog lists 150 CUP for foreigners (undated), well under a dollar at the street rate, but dual pricing may apply, so check the price.

places.name: Mural de la Prehistoria
places.note: A 120 m cliff painted with dinosaurs in 1961 on Castro's suggestion; you can see it from the road for free, and the entry only buys you a closer look at the same paint.

places.name: El Olivo
places.note: The Mediterranean paladar on the main street, lamb and pasta when they have it, with a queue at 19:30 on the nights the town has power; go at 18:00.

places.name: 3J Tapas Bar
places.note: The bar the guides drink in, tapas plates and cheap rum on the main street; the kitchen shrinks with the shortages so order what the board says, not the menu.

places.name: Centro Cultural Polo Montañez
places.note: The open-air patio on the square with a live band and salsa from about 22:00; it is the only night out in town and it goes dark when the grid does.

places.name: Cayo Jutías
places.note: The best beach day in the west, 90 minutes each way on a broken road in a shared taxi from your casa; bring your own lunch and water because the bar sells out.

places.name: Finca Agroecológica El Paraíso
places.note: An organic farm on a hill above town serving a fixed feast of what they grew, with a valley view from the table; busloads once filled it, and now it is mostly empty and better for it.

places.name: Plaza Mayor and the cobbled streets
places.note: The square, the yellow church, and the grid of 18th century houses around it, walked at 8am before the heat and the jineteros; the whole colonial core is 20 minutes end to end.

places.name: Museo Histórico Municipal (Palacio Cantero) tower
places.note: A sugar baron's mansion with a wooden tower that gives the best view of the red roofs and the Escambray; the rooms are thin, the climb is the point, and closing day has moved between Friday and Monday, so check at your casa.

places.name: Casa de la Música steps
places.note: A salsa band on the stone stairway off Plaza Mayor most nights from 22:00, free to sit on the steps and a couple of dollars for a mojito; it is the one thing every visitor does and it is still good.

places.name: Taberna La Canchánchara
places.note: The rum, honey and lime drink in a clay cup that this bar exists to serve, with a trio playing to a courtyard of tour groups; one drink at 17:00 and out.

places.name: Playa Ancón
places.note: The south coast beach 15 minutes by taxi or 50 by bicycle, calm and shallow with a state hotel at one end you should not use; after summer 2026 the local paper called it a sea of rubbish, so ask your casa about its state that week and fall back on La Boca.

places.name: Torre Manaca Iznaga
places.note: The 45 m tower built in 1816 to watch the enslaved workers in the cane fields, climbable for a small fee, with the estate house now a state restaurant to skip; the lane below is wall to wall lace sellers.

places.name: Salto del Caburní, Topes de Collantes
places.note: A 4x4 taxi up into the mountains (35 to 40 dollars per car return), park entry of about 10 dollars, then a steep 5 km round trip to a waterfall pool; the climb out in the afternoon heat is hard, carry two litres each.

places.name: Restaurante San José
places.note: The reliable paladar a block off Maceo, big plates of fish, shrimp and pork with a generator humming when the town is dark; AlaMesa's 2026 band is 8 to 14 dollars. Daily 12:00 to 23:00 and the 20:00 wait can be 30 minutes, so go at 18:30.

places.name: Taberna La Botija
places.note: A tavern decorated with slave-era iron and open until 2am with live music, tapas and a long rum list; the late kitchen makes it the place for the night the colectivo arrives at 21:00.

places.name: Palenque de los Congos Reales
places.note: The Afro-Cuban folkloric group's own courtyard, a block from the Casa de la Música steps, with rumba and drum sets some evenings around 22:00; the schedule is chalked on the door that afternoon, so look on your way past.

places.name: Disco Ayala
places.note: A nightclub inside a cave on the hill above town, reggaeton and a fog machine at a state-run bar; the walk up in the dark is the only interesting part.

places.name: Parque José Martí
places.note: The French-laid square of a city founded in 1819 by settlers from Bordeaux and Louisiana, ringed by the cathedral, the town hall and the Terry theatre; the arch at the west end is the only triumphal arch in Cuba and it takes an hour to see it all.

places.name: Teatro Tomás Terry
places.note: An 1890 horseshoe theatre with Carrara marble, a painted ceiling and cedar seats, open for a paid look when there is no rehearsal; Caruso sang here and it still hosts shows when the power allows.

places.name: Palacio de Valle rooftop bar
places.note: A 1917 Moorish fantasy house at the end of the peninsula, a historical landmark now run as a state restaurant to skip; go up for a mojito on the roof terrace with the bay at sunset. Hours vary, check, and check it is not on the Restricted List: it sits in the Hotel Jagua grounds.

places.name: Malecón and Paseo del Prado to Punta Gorda
places.note: The city's long straight boulevard becomes the sea wall and ends at the wooden houses on the tip of the peninsula; locals do this at dusk and the breeze is the only air conditioning in a blackout.

places.name: Castillo de Jagua by ferry
places.note: A 1745 Spanish fort guarding the bay mouth, 50 pesos in 2024, reached by the passenger ferry from the Avenida 46 dock (about 08:00 and 13:00, 30 minutes, cash in pesos). Fort 09:30 to 17:00, Sunday to 13:00, hours vary, check; confirm the return boat before you board.

places.name: El Nicho
places.note: The Escambray's best swimming, a chain of pools and falls on an easy 1.5 km loop, 90 minutes each way with the last stretch rough; a taxi is 60 to 80 dollars per car, so find two other people at your casa.

places.name: Playa Rancho Luna
places.note: A workable brown-sand beach 25 minutes from Punta Gorda by taxi, with a state hotel behind it you do not use; the water is clear and it is the easy half day if El Nicho is too much.

places.name: Paladar Aché
places.note: A family paladar on a garden patio on the Prado (Avenida 38), roast pork, grilled fish and vegetarian plates when the market allows, daily 12:00 to 22:00. AlaMesa's 2026 band is 22 to 28 dollars a head, so bring more than the old 14.

places.name: Camila's Restaurant
places.note: Seafood and lobster on a terrace out at La Punta, the local pick for a bay-side dinner. A Google reviewer quoted a 10 dollar menu in Dec 2025; listed hours differ (07:00 to 22:00 against 12:00 to 23:00), so hours vary, check.

places.name: Jardín Botánico de Cienfuegos
places.note: A 94 hectare Harvard-founded garden from 1901 with 2,000 plant species and a bamboo grove, taxied to in 25 minutes (20 dollars return); the labels are faded and the paths untended, and that is part of it.

places.name: Playa Larga village beach
places.note: A short strip of pale sand at the head of the bay, calm and warm, right outside the casas; it is a village beach with fishermen and kids, not a resort, and the sunset from it is the reason to stay the night.

places.name: Cueva de los Peces
places.note: A 70 m deep flooded cenote 50 m from the road with a reef straight across the tarmac, so you snorkel the sinkhole and then the sea from the same car park; masks rent for 3 dollars and the restaurant is state-run and slow.

places.name: Punta Perdiz
places.note: The best shore snorkel in Cuba, a coral shelf and the wreck of a 1961 landing craft dropping to a blue wall 30 m out; the dive centre does a 25 dollar tank dive, and the all-inclusive lunch and drinks day pass at the state bar is about 15 dollars.

places.name: Museo Girón
places.note: The Cuban account of the April 1961 invasion in two large rooms, with ex-WWII vehicles and a Sea Fury outside and some English captions; an hour is enough. The 08:00 to 17:00 hours and 3 dollar ticket are not confirmed for 2025-26, so check the price.

places.name: Caleta Buena
places.note: A rock-ringed cove of clear water with ladders down into it at Playa Maceo, east of Giron. A reviewer paid 15 dollars for the day pass with lunch and drinks, 10:00 to 16:00 (undated), so check the price; the lunch is rice and whatever fish came in.

places.name: Las Salinas de Brito
places.note: Salt flats inside the national park where flamingos, spoonbills and herons feed at dawn, entered only with a park guide booked the day before at the office in Playa Larga or through your casa; 6am start, back by 11 when the heat and the birds go.

places.name: Sendero Bermejas
places.note: A flat forest trail where the guides find the Cuban trogon, tody and the bee hummingbird, the smallest bird there is; guide obligatory and worth it, and the mosquitoes are worst here of anywhere on the trip.
places.neighborhood: Ciénaga de Zapata, road to Girón

places.name: Casa Enrique dinner
places.note: The Rivas family's casa at Caleton has served lobster, crab and fish dinners to guests, ordered by 16:00, but the only page found dates from 2015. The casa could not be confirmed for 2025-26, so check before counting on dinner there.

places.name: Criadero de Cocodrilos, Boca de Guamá
places.note: A state crocodile farm on the main road with pens of animals, photos with a taped-mouth baby and a boat to a fake Taíno village on the lake; it is the coach stop, and the swamp guides show you the real thing for the same money.

places.name: Mausoleo del Che Guevara
places.note: The bronze statue, the small museum of his letters and rifles, and the crypt with an eternal flame where he and 16 comrades from Bolivia were reburied in 1997; free, no bags or photos inside, and the Monday closure is enforced.

places.name: Monumento a la Toma del Tren Blindado
places.note: Four carriages of the armoured train Che's men derailed with a bulldozer on 29 December 1958, the fight that ended Batista, kept where they fell with the bulldozer on a plinth; 20 minutes of exhibits and a walk along the track.
places.neighborhood: Line to Camajuaní, east of centre

places.name: Parque Vidal
places.note: The square the whole city circles in the evening, once with separate pavements for black and white citizens, with a bandstand and the Caridad theatre on it; sit with a peso coffee and watch a provincial city that gets few visitors now.

places.name: Teatro La Caridad
places.note: An 1885 theatre paid for by the town benefactress Marta Abreu, with a painted ceiling and marble lobby, open for a short look for a small fee when nothing is on; ten minutes inside is the visit.

places.name: Club Mejunje
places.note: A ruined-house courtyard cultural centre that has run rock, trova, rumba and Cuba's first drag shows since 1991; the Sunday afternoon and Saturday night programmes are the ones, and it only matters if you are here late in the day.

places.name: Loma del Capiro
places.note: The hill Che used as his command post in the battle for the city, a 20 minute walk up from the train monument for a view over Santa Clara to the Escambray; there is a flag and a plaque and nobody else.

places.name: The Boulevard (Calle Independencia)
places.note: The pedestrian shopping street east of Parque Vidal where the private MSME shops and the peso cafes are; it shows what the city buys and what is missing better than any museum.

places.name: Florida Center
places.note: Dinner in the plant-filled colonial courtyard of the best-known casa in town, lamb or fish with proper vegetables, for guests and outsiders who book by the afternoon; if you are only here for the day, ask whether they will serve lunch.

places.name: Museo de Artes Decorativas
places.note: An 18th century townhouse on the square filled with the furniture, porcelain and glass of the sugar families, small enough for 30 minutes and cooler than the street; hours drift with the staff and the power, so treat the times as a guide.

places.name: Museo de la Revolución
places.note: The former Presidential Palace, with Che's gun and cap inside and the Granma boat outside; labels are Spanish only and renovation limits access, some visitors see only the annex. Closed Mondays, roughly 5 to 10 dollars, pay in CUP cash, go early.

places.name: Castillo de los Tres Reyes del Morro
places.note: Built 1587 to 1597 to guard the harbour mouth, with the lighthouse and the best sea view of the city. Daily 10:00 to 19:00, check the price; pair it with the 21:00 cannon at La Cabaña next door and skip the shops.
places.neighborhood: Habana del Este, across the harbour

places.name: Capitolio
places.note: The 1929 seat of government until 1959, seen only on guided tours Wednesday to Saturday at 10:00, 11:00 and 14:00 (2025). Buy at the office across the street with your passport, no cash inside, check the price.

places.name: Gran Teatro de La Habana Alicia Alonso
places.note: The neo-baroque home of the national ballet, opened 1915, toured with a guide and a roof view of the Capitolio. Listed days differ, so go Tuesday to Saturday 10:00 to 16:00; a 2025 visitor paid 600 pesos, check the price, and parts may be under restoration.

places.name: Museo del Ron Havana Club
places.note: Rum history with a scale model of a factory and a tasting at the end, booked at the entrance. Hours vary, check, and check the price of the tour and tasting packages before you sign up.

places.name: Castillo de San Salvador de la Punta
places.note: The 1590s fort facing El Morro across the harbour mouth, damaged in the British siege of 1762, at the start of the Malecón. Hours vary, check, and check the price; go early.

places.name: La Cuenca
places.note: Lasagne, Cuban sandwiches and a terrace for drinks on the main street, with wifi that works; service is uneven. AlaMesa 2026 band 8 to 14 dollars, and prices change with the rate they apply, so check.

places.name: Gran Caverna de Santo Tomás
places.note: Cuba's largest cave system, about 47 km, toured with helmet and lamp after a steep 20 minute climb and a ladder; a 2022 hurricane damaged the usual route. Last tour 15:30, hours vary, check it is open and check the price.
places.neighborhood: Minas de Matahambre road, 20 km west

places.name: Jardín Botánico de Viñales
places.note: A family garden of native plants, old trees and fruit with hummingbirds and parrots, walked with a guide, daily 08:00 to 19:00. Free with a donation expected (2019 review); the criollo lunch there is extra.

places.name: Los Conspiradores
places.note: The busy paladar on Calle Cristo by the Plaza Mayor, Google 4.8 from 1,592 reviews, taking euros, dollars or pesos. AlaMesa 2026 band 8 to 14 dollars a head; book a table for 19:00.

places.name: La Esquina 373
places.note: A corner paladar on Rosario a block from the Plaza Mayor that reviewers call good value, though AlaMesa's 2026 band starts at 29 dollars a head, the top of town. Sources disagree on opening times, hours vary, check.

places.name: Casa de la Trova
places.note: The trova house on Calle Cristo, live son and guitar music with a bar, a separate venue from the Casa de la Música steps nearby. Hours vary, check, and check the price of the cover at the door.

places.name: Casa Prado
places.note: A Prado paladar with big portions; order the special paella or the fish fillet. AlaMesa 2026 band 8 to 14 dollars a head, a bit above the rest of town, daily 11:30 to 22:30.

places.name: Bar-Restaurante Doña Nora
places.note: A bar and dining room on the Prado known for lamb and rabbit in wine, the cheaper dinner in town: AlaMesa's 2026 band is 7 dollars and under. Daily 11:30 to 23:00.

places.name: Chuchi El Pescador
places.note: A seafood shack; order the Filete Playa Larga, the Maria la Gorda fish and lobster plate, or the cigua sea snails. A 2023 Tripadvisor forum post put a lobster dinner at 7 to 8 USD or EUR, so confirm the price at the door.

places.name: Restaurante El Mora
places.note: Google 4.9 from 381 reviews and open daily. A 2024 HappyCow review paid 700 pesos for a vegetarian dish, about 1.40 dollars at the 2026 street rate; lobster costs far more, and blackouts happen.

places.name: Museo Romántico (Palacio Brunet)
places.note: The Brunet sugar family's 1704 mansion, a museum since 1974: 14 rooms of European furniture, porcelain and silver, and the upstairs balcony over the plaza. 08:30 to 16:45, shut Mondays, 45 minutes; check the price, and go at opening before the tour groups.

places.name: Museo de Arquitectura Colonial
places.note: The doors, grilles, locks and hinges that built the 18th and 19th century town, in the sky-blue Sánchez Iznaga house; see the garden patio. Tuesday to Saturday 09:00 to 16:00, Sunday to 12:00, shut Mondays, hours vary, check. Check the price; guides often speak Spanish only.

places.name: Museo de Arqueología Guamuhaya
places.note: The only look at Trinidad before the Spanish: Taíno and Guamuhaya artefacts plus natural science, in the pale-yellow building on the plaza. 09:00 to 17:00, shut Mondays, half an hour; check the price.
places.neighborhood: Plaza Mayor, Calle Real del Jigüe 95

places.name: Museo de la Lucha Contra Bandidos and bell tower
places.note: The 1960s Escambray war against the counter-revolutionaries, photos and weapons in the old Franciscan convent; climb the yellow bell tower for the second-best roof view in town. Tuesday to Sunday 09:00 to 17:00, hours vary, check; check the price.
places.neighborhood: Convento de San Francisco, Calle Cristo 274

places.name: Iglesia Parroquial de la Santísima Trinidad
places.note: The Parroquial Mayor on the plaza, consecrated in 1892 to replace a 17th century church lost to a hurricane; look at the hardwood altars and colonial icons. Monday to Saturday 10:30 to 13:00, hours vary, check; check the price.

places.name: Catedral de la Purísima Concepción
places.note: The neoclassical cathedral on Parque Martí, from the second half of the 19th century, with lions at the door and French stained glass, the thing to see inside; John Paul II came here. Hours vary, check; check the price. Twenty minutes in the morning.

places.name: Palacio Ferrer, Museo de las Artes
places.note: The 1920 Catalan-modernist house of sugar magnate José Ferrer Sires, now a cultural palace with local art; climb to the rooftop cupola for the view over the city. Hours vary, check; check the price.

places.name: Museo Histórico Naval Nacional
places.note: A rose-pink building founded as a museum in 1933, with pre-colonial finds, colonial pieces and the navy's story, the 1957 Cienfuegos uprising included. 09:00 to 16:00 daily but it can close at times; one reviewer got in free, check the price.

places.name: Palacio de Gobierno (Ayuntamiento)
places.note: The early 1900s provincial government palace with a Moorish touch, part of the UNESCO square beside the cathedral. Free from outside, and you can look in at the staircase, 08:00 to 17:00 daily; 15 minutes.

places.name: Arco de Triunfo
places.note: The independence monument on Parque Martí, the square's only memorial to the wars of independence, in front of Palacio Ferrer. Free and open-air, ten minutes, best in the evening light.

places.name: Muelle Real
places.note: The old Muelle Circular pier, a historic landmark turned into a quiet waterfront with egrets and a bar nearby. Free; come for half an hour at sunset.

places.name: Cementerio Tomás Acea
places.note: A garden cemetery founded in 1902 behind a 1926 Parthenon-style gate with a Doric pavilion; find the monument to the martyrs of the 1957 naval uprising. Hours vary, check; check the price. Go in the morning.

places.name: Museo Municipal Adela Azcuy
places.note: The only museum in town, small and on local history, and the start of guided valley hikes at about 09:30. Hours vary, check; one reviewer got in free, check the price.

places.name: Palenque de los Cimarrones (Cueva de San Miguel)
places.note: Walk through the San Miguel cave to the palenque, the hideout where runaway slaves sheltered, now a restaurant and bar at the cave exit. Caves 09:00 to 17:30 daily, 120 pesos in 2023; an hour, by day.
places.neighborhood: North of town, Cueva del Indio road

places.name: Casa del Veguero
places.note: A working tobacco farm on the Pinar del Río road where farmers roll cigars in front of you, listed on Google as a restaurant and priced for tourists. Hours vary, check; check the price.

outings.why: A slow loop through tobacco fields under the mogotes with stops at a drying house, a coffee finca and a swimming hole; the horses are tired and the guides push cigar sales at every stop, so agree the route and the price first.
outings.name: Valle del Silencio on horseback
outings.season: All year; tobacco is in the ground December to March
outings.fallback: Walk the same lanes from the end of Calle Adela Azcuy for free, 2 hours.

outings.why: A steady climb on a farm track to a hillside hamlet founded by a water-cure sect in the 1940s, with the whole valley below and a family that serves coffee on the porch; hot and unshaded after 10am, start at 8.
outings.name: Los Acuáticos walk
outings.fallback: Mirador Los Jazmines by taxi, 1 hour.

outings.why: A white sand key 65 km northwest reached by a causeway, with shallow clear water and almost nobody on it now; the road is bad, the taxi takes 90 minutes each way, and the snack bar runs out of everything by 2pm, so bring food and water.
outings.name: Cayo Jutías
outings.season: All year; November to April for calm water
outings.fallback: Cueva del Indio and Finca Raúl Reyes, 3 hours.

outings.why: The main Topes de Collantes trail: a 45 minute 4x4 taxi climb into the Escambray, then a steep 2.5 km each way down to a 60 m waterfall and cold pool, and the climb back out in the heat is what people remember; the park entry is paid in cas
outings.name: Salto del Caburní
outings.season: All year; fullest after rains June to October
outings.fallback: Parque El Cubano and Salto de Javira, 15 minutes from town, 3 hours.

outings.why: The sugar valley that paid for Trinidad, seen from the mirador and then from the top of the 45 m slave-watch tower at the Iznaga estate; the tourist steam train has not run reliably in years, so go by taxi (20 to 25 dollars return) and expe
outings.name: Valle de los Ingenios and Manaca Iznaga
outings.fallback: The mirador alone by taxi, 90 minutes.

outings.why: The south coast beach 12 km from town, wide and shallow, reached by bicycle in 50 minutes or taxi in 15; in September 2026 the provincial paper described it as buried in rubbish after the summer, so look before you commit and keep La Boca i
outings.name: Playa Ancón
outings.fallback: La Boca fishing village beach, 7 km, 3 hours.

outings.why: A 1.5 km loop of waterfalls and swimming pools on the Cienfuegos side of the Escambray, better water than Caburní and an easier walk, but the last 20 km of road are rough and the taxi (60 to 80 dollars per car, split it) is most of the cost
outings.name: El Nicho
outings.season: All year; strongest flow June to November
outings.fallback: Rancho Luna beach, 18 km from Cienfuegos, 4 hours.

outings.why: The reef wall starts 30 m off the road along the bay, so a taxi (or the dive centre truck) drops you at Cueva de los Peces and then Punta Perdiz for shore snorkelling over coral, a sunken landing craft and 300 m of blue drop-off; masks rent
outings.name: The Bay of Pigs snorkel run
outings.season: All year; best visibility December to April

outings.why: Flamingos, spoonbills and the Cuban trogon on the salt flats of the Zapata swamp, entered only with a licensed park guide arranged the day before through your casa; start at 6am because the birds and the shade both leave by 10.
outings.name: Las Salinas de Brito birding
outings.season: November to April for migrants; flamingos most of the year

outings.why: Soldiers in 18th century dress fire a cannon over the harbour at 9pm every night from the fortress across the bay; go over by taxi at 7:30 for the rampart views of a mostly dark city, and expect the ceremony itself to take 15 minutes.

destination.name: Cuba
destination.pitch: Cuba in 2026 is a country in a fuel and grid crisis with tourism down by more than half, so you go for the people, the music and the tobacco valley, you sleep in casas with inverters and water tanks, and you accept dark evenings as part of
destination.caveat: US law bars tourist travel: you need one of the 12 OFAC general licence categories, usually Support for the Cuban People, so casas and paladares only and no hotel on the Prohibited Accommodations list. The State Department advisory read Level 2 when checked, and power cuts run up to 12 hours a day. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Habana Vieja and the Malecón still carry the trip, but Vedado at night is now mostly dark.
because.food: The casa breakfast and a handful of paladares are good; everything else is rationed, repetitive and improvised, and shortages hit menus daily.
because.nature: The Viñales mogotes, the Escambray waterfalls and the reef right off the road at the Bay of Pigs are real and cheap, and the crowds that used to fill them are gone.
because.culture: Rumba in a Centro Habana alley, son on the Trinidad steps, the Che mausoleum, and conversations with casa owners about what the year has been like.
because.adventure: Snorkelling a 1961 landing craft at Punta Perdiz, horses through Valle del Silencio and a colectivo ride with a driver hunting for petrol.
because.relaxation: Only at Playa Larga or on a Viñales porch with a rocking chair, and only if you do not need air conditioning at 2am.
because.exploration: Each town is a different century, the transport is a negotiation, and half the trip is figuring out what is open today.
